records.title: fix(server): reuse Git index metadata during checkpoint capture
records.body:
## What Changed

Checkpoint capture now seeds its private index from the workspace index and resets it to HEAD while retaining matching file metadata. The existing `git add -A -- .` then avoids rereading unchanged tracked files. The workspace index stays untouched.

Discard filesystem-monitor state during the reset. Fall back to the existing fresh-index path if copying or inspection fails, inspection is truncated, or assume-unchanged/skip-worktree flags remain.

## Why

Starting with a fresh index throws away Git's stat cache on every capture. Reusing it reduces unnecessary work in large repositories while preserving scoped staging and snapshot contents.

Related to #3646; independent of the failed-write cleanup in #9809. Builds on the index-reuse approach explored in #8538, with a fresh-index fallback instead of normalizing special flags. Unlike #8301, this keeps native `add -A` staging rather than parsing changed paths. Discussion: https://github.com/pingdotgg/t3code/discussions/9808#discussioncomment-18351271.

## Validation

- 38 tests pass across GitVcsDriver, CheckpointStore, and VcsProcess; server typecheck, targeted lint, and formatting pass.
- The unchanged-file clean-filter regression fails on main and passes here. Tests cover two consecutive captures at root/nested directories, staged/unstaged/deleted/untracked files, special flags, split indexes, missing/corrupt indexes, and an unchanged workspace index.
- Five paired complete captures on a 40,000-file fixture (10 modified, one untracked): median **242.5 ms → 74.1 ms (about 3.3× faster)**. Every paired snapshot tree matched and the workspace index remained byte-identical. Baseline: `061543e9e`.

The 30-second timeout is unchanged. Large new or modified files still need hashing; this does not claim to resolve every timeout in #3646.

## Checklist

- [x] This PR is small and focused
- [x] I explained what changed and why

Implemented and verified with GPT-6 Astra through the Codex harness.


<!-- This is an auto-generated comment: release notes by coderabbit.ai -->

## Summary by CodeRabbit

- **Bug Fixes**
  - Checkpoint capture now preserves existing file state more reliably, including staged, deleted, newly added, and specially tracked files.
  - Improved handling of missing or invalid Git index states, with graceful fallback behavior.
  - Avoided unnecessary filter processing for unchanged indexed files during checkpoint capture.
  - Checkpoint reuse now better preserves the original index across different repository configurations.

records.title: fix(server): reuse index stat cache for checkpoints
records.body:
<!--

You can still open a PR, but please do so knowing there is a high chance
we may close it without merging it, or never review it.

- Small, focused PRs are strongly preferred. Bug fixes are most likely to be merged.
- New features will most likely just annoy us.
- 1,000+ line PRs with a bunch of new features will probably get you banned from the repo.
-->

## What Changed

<!-- Describe the change clearly and keep scope tight. -->

Seed the temporary checkpoint index from the current worktree's index, then use a single-tree `read-tree --reset HEAD` to reuse matching stat entries without borrowing the user's staged snapshot. The scoped `git add -A -- .`, tree/commit creation, and checkpoint ref publication stay unchanged.

Preserve the source index timestamp so copying cannot hide racy-clean edits. Use the previous fresh-index path for sparse/split indexes, assume-unchanged/skip-worktree entries, truncated listings, unavailable indexes, or failed seeding. Unborn repositories keep the existing empty-index behavior. The real index is never modified.

## Why

<!-- Explain the problem being solved and why this approach is the right one. -->

A fresh `read-tree HEAD` discards the stat cache, forcing checkpoint staging to reread unchanged tracked files. On a Linux workspace with 32,981 tracked files (448 MB), staging initially took 66.9 seconds and exceeded the existing 30-second timeout.

Related to #3646. Alternative to #8301: reuse Git's index cache rather than parse changed paths and introduce binary process I/O plumbing. This does not address failure backoff or temporary-pack cleanup, and intentionally does not accelerate special-index fallback cases.

Validation:
- 62 focused tests pass across `GitVcsDriver.test.ts`, `CheckpointStore.test.ts`, and `CheckpointReactor.test.ts`.
- A counting clean-filter regression fails on upstream and passes with this change: unchanged files are not filtered again, while changed content is captured.
- A racy-clean regression fails if timestamp preservation is removed and passes with it.
- Real Git fixtures compare snapshot trees against the original algorithm and verify byte-identical user indexes across partial staging, staged deletions/AD paths, intent-to-add, subdirectory scope, unborn HEAD, missing indexes, linked worktrees, flags, sparse/split indexes, and unmerged entries. Capture/restore is also exercised.
- Targeted lint and `git diff --check` pass.
- Server typecheck reports the same two TS2345 errors on both unmodified base `eb1150636` and this change: `HostPowerMonitor.ts:69` and `NativeTelemetryClient.ts:509`. No errors in modified files.
- Final same-run Linux comparison using bundled original/modified drivers and isolated Git metadata/objects: full capture plus tree lookup took **2.771 s → 0.386 s** (~7.2× faster), with identical tree OIDs and an unchanged real index. This later run did not reproduce the initial 66.9 s staging time; the initial and later measurements are not a controlled before/after pair. No installed T3 server was replaced.
- A Linux fixture verified changed content under a non-UTF-8 filename survives capture.
- macOS Git 2.55.0 tested locally; Linux Git 2.43.0 tested through an isolated actual-driver harness. Windows was not tested.

## Checklist

- [x] I explained what changed and why
- [ ] I included before/after screenshots for any UI changes (N/A: server-only)
- [ ] I included a video for animation/interaction changes (N/A: no UI interaction changes)

records.title: fix(web): tone the SnapShot overlay from the captured image
records.body:
## What Changed

The SnapShot attachment overlay (app icon, app name, window title) was hardcoded to a black-to-transparent gradient with white text, so it clashed with the surrounding card in light mode. Swapping to a theme-colored gradient did not help either: a dark terminal in light mode got a white smear, a light window in dark mode got a black one. The overlay's background is the captured image, not the app theme.

The overlay now takes its tone from the image it sits on:

- A small helper (`snapShotOverlayTone.ts`) loads the thumbnail once per URL, takes the centered crop that `object-cover` shows in the 52:28 frame, draws that crop's bottom band into a 16×4 canvas so the rasterizer averages it, and reads the mean color.
- The scrim gradient extends that color, pushed 35% toward black or white away from mid-tones, and the label picks white or near-black text at the equal-contrast luminance threshold.
- Values are applied as CSS variables on the overlay. The sampled state is keyed to the URL it came from, so a thumbnail that swaps from its blob preview to the uploaded asset never wears the previous image's tone. Until the sample lands, or when the canvas cannot be read, the overlay keeps the black gradient it had on `main`.
- The composer thumbnail, the timeline image, and the expanded image dialog share the one component and now pass the thumbnail URL in. No contract changes; existing captures get this immediately.
- `Button` gains an `overlay` variant that inherits `currentColor` and tints its hover from it. The accessibility-contents button uses it, so the overlay sets the button's tone through its own text color with no call-site color classes.

## Why

Light mode users saw a dark bar on every SnapShot, and any single fixed color is wrong for half of all captures.

## UI Changes

Captured in the web client, same thread, viewport, and scroll position. Only the emulated color scheme and the captured image differ. The light capture is a real attachment from the same thread substituted into the SnapShot slot.

**Before, on `main`** (black gradient regardless of theme or image):

| Light mode | Dark mode |
| --- | --- |
| ![Before, light mode: black gradient with white text over the dark Ghostty capture](https://gh-file-drop-api-prod-mi5fy3sowv63ufte.pinglabs.workers.dev/f/b2bd4574a9c97531/before-light.png) | ![Before, dark mode: black gradient with white text over the dark Ghostty capture](https://gh-file-drop-api-prod-mi5fy3sowv63ufte.pinglabs.workers.dev/f/d2c8ce171fcf35ca/before-dark.png) |

**After** (sampled from the image):

| | Light mode | Dark mode |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Dark capture (Ghostty) | ![After, light mode, dark capture: blue-black scrim with white text](https://gh-file-drop-api-prod-mi5fy3sowv63ufte.pinglabs.workers.dev/f/b03190b108d2577e/sample-light.png) | ![After, dark mode, dark capture: blue-black scrim with white text](https://gh-file-drop-api-prod-mi5fy3sowv63ufte.pinglabs.workers.dev/f/052e087bf76f3f6f/sample-dark.png) |
| Light capture (T3 Code) | ![After, light mode, light capture: near-white scrim with dark text](https://gh-file-drop-api-prod-mi5fy3sowv63ufte.pinglabs.workers.dev/f/faefa4f1061dd9e8/sample-lightimg-light.png) | ![After, dark mode, light capture: near-white scrim with dark text](https://gh-file-drop-api-prod-mi5fy3sowv63ufte.pinglabs.workers.dev/f/66241db2018d1b8c/sample-lightimg-dark.png) |

### Broader sample

Two captures are not much of a test, so I surveyed all 221 PNG attachments in a real database, measured the bottom band each one would show in the 52:28 frame, and seeded 14 of them as SnapShots on one message to cover the space: pure black, dark neutral, dark saturated blue, both sides of the text-color threshold, true mid gray, saturated blue, purple, light gray, warm off-white, pure white, a 9:1 ultra-wide strip, and tall dark and light portraits. Each card's subtitle carries the measured luminance, mean color, and source size.

The survey rows are seeded projection data in a disposable worktree copy, not real captures, so the app icons show the fallback initial. Same viewport, scroll, and data in all four grids.

| Before, light mode | Before, dark mode |
| --- | --- |
| ![Before survey, light mode: every card wears the same black gradient with white text](https://gh-file-drop-api-prod-mi5fy3sowv63ufte.pinglabs.workers.dev/f/275e12070dd97907/survey-before-light.png) | ![Before survey, dark mode: every card wears the same black gradient with white text](https://gh-file-drop-api-prod-mi5fy3sowv63ufte.pinglabs.workers.dev/f/5af1cd9c211f5094/survey-before-dark.png) |

| After, light mode | After, dark mode |
| --- | --- |
| ![After survey, light mode: each card's scrim extends its own bottom color, text flips at the threshold](https://gh-file-drop-api-prod-mi5fy3sowv63ufte.pinglabs.workers.dev/f/c1d7d86862486117/survey-light.png) | ![After survey, dark mode: identical tones to light mode, since the image decides](https://gh-file-drop-api-prod-mi5fy3sowv63ufte.pinglabs.workers.dev/f/7d32cfb86ea816f9/survey-dark.png) |

Sampled values read back from the DOM (scrim / text), identical in both themes:

| Case | Measured band | Scrim | Text |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 00 black wide | lum 0.000 | `rgb(1 1 1)` | white |
| 01 dark neutral | lum 0.005 | `rgb(11 11 11)` | white |
| 02 dark blue | lum 0.107, sat 88 | `rgb(33 64 99)` | white |
| 03 just below threshold | lum 0.154 | `rgb(168 168 170)` | dark |
| 04 just above threshold | lum 0.285 | `rgb(176 176 177)` | dark |
| 05 mid gray | lum 0.337 | `rgb(178 178 178)` | dark |
| 06 saturated blue portrait | lum 0.351, sat 160 | `rgb(135 191 252)` | dark |
| 07 purple portrait | lum 0.157, sat 43 | `rgb(75 56 85)` | white |
| 08 light gray | lum 0.608 | `rgb(228 227 231)` | dark |
| 09 warm off-white | lum 0.974 | `rgb(253 254 247)` | dark |
| 10 white | lum 1.000 | `rgb(255 255 255)` | dark |
| 11 ultra-wide | lum 0.011 | `rgb(18 18 18)` | white |
| 12 tall dark portrait | lum 0.003 | `rgb(7 7 7)` | white |
| 13 tall light portrait | lum 0.939 | `rgb(250 250 250)` | dark |

Two things worth knowing from this. Case 03 was measured just under the threshold from the full source image, but the sampler reads the visible cover crop, which lands on a lighter region, so it correctly went to dark text. The survey band is the bottom 30% of the crop, while the survey table measured the full bottom band, so the two agree on direction but not on exact numbers. And the mid-gray cases (04, 05) are the weakest of the set: a 35% push toward white on `rgb(157,157,157)` gives `rgb(178,178,178)`, which is legible but low-contrast against the gray image above it. A stronger push for mid-tones is a one-constant change if that matters.

## Verification

- `snapShotOverlayTone.test.ts` (9 new tests) covers text selection around the luminance threshold, scrim direction, hue preservation, alpha-weighted averaging, and the cover crop for frame-shaped, portrait, and ultra-wide sources. `SnapShotAttachmentDetails.test.tsx` (4 tests) still passes.
- Web typecheck passes. Lint is clean on the new files; the one warning on the existing file is on an untouched line.
- Sampled values observed in the browser: the Ghostty capture produced `rgb(26 29 34)` with white text, the T3 Code capture produced `rgb(252 252 252)` with `rgb(24 24 27)` text.
- Desktop wraps the web client and gets the same behavior. Mobile has no SnapShot overlay.

**Remote connections.** In dev the asset URL is same-origin through the Vite proxy, so the cross-origin read path was not exercised end to end. The backend's CORS middleware is global and the asset route answered a foreign-origin preflight with 204 here. If a remote origin is ever refused, the canvas taints, the read throws, and the overlay keeps the black fallback, which is today's behavior. Worth one look on a real app.t3.codes or tunnel connection.

Implemented with Claude Fable 5.1 in Claude Code.

- [x] I included before/after screenshots for any UI changes
- [ ] I included a video for animation/interaction changes (not applicable)

records.title: [Bug]: SnapShot animation leaves an oversized bar on Hyprland
records.body:
### Before submitting

- [x] I searched existing issues and did not find a duplicate.
- [x] I included enough detail to reproduce or investigate the problem.

### Area

apps/desktop

### Steps to reproduce

1. On Omarchy / Hyprland 0.56.2, enable SnapShots and Capture animations in the desktop app.
2. Capture another app on the same monitor as T3 Code.
3. Repeat with the captured app on another monitor.
4. Watch the screenshot shrink into the composer before the animation overlay disappears.

### Expected behavior

The overlay shrinks to the attachment bounds without drawing outside the thumbnail.

### Actual behavior

The thumbnail shrinks, but an oversized solid rectangle remains behind it until the overlay is removed. On the same monitor it can be wide; across monitors it can become a narrow vertical strip. The reported bar is black. A synthetic checkerboard with a white border reproduces a white rectangle, so the color depends on the image.

The finished attachment is correct. This affects the temporary animation only.

### Impact

Cosmetic issue

### Version or commit

Introduced with #8103. Reproduced with the installed Nightly helper and a helper built from main at 8588d7f63.

### Environment

Omarchy 4 development branch, Hyprland 0.56.2, native Wayland. Two 1920x1080 monitors at scale 1.

### Investigation

The helper updates the viewport size without reattaching its unchanged image buffer. Hyprland 0.56.2 copies the surface size only on a buffer update, leaving the previous dimensions around the newly scaled image. Reattaching the same buffer during resizing removes the artifact in both same-monitor and cross-monitor replay tests.

### Workaround

Turn off Capture animations in Settings > SnapShots.

records.title: fix: share native app icons across tool activity and snapshots
records.body: Computer-use activity could lose app names and show generic icons, including macOS apps whose icons live in asset catalogs. Native app lookup and cached PNG rendering now live in one shared helper used by tool activity and SnapShots. The server resolves app IDs or display names on the environment that ran the tool. SnapShots passes the app path its existing macOS/Windows foreground-window code already discovers. Windows uses the Shell image API in a bounded PowerShell subprocess, so icon extraction works without Electron. SnapShots retains its existing Electron fallback, and Linux keeps its existing behavior. SnapShots' existing foreground-app discovery is reused, but its icon extraction depends on Electron APIs. Moving that helper into a shared package would not make those APIs available to a standalone Node server. A remote desktop client cannot supply the server's local app icons either. The shared resolver therefore uses native macOS and Windows extraction on the environment that owns the app, while desktop retains its Electron fallback. Desktop-only support could reuse the Electron helper directly; standalone server support requires this native extraction path. The adapter preserves app-name precedence and waits at most 250 ms for native name enrichment so it cannot hold up provider events. The lookup itself keeps running in the session scope, because interrupting it would evict the pending cache entry and a slow first lookup would never warm the cache; the next event for that app reads the resolved name. Repeat events share the in-flight lookup, and a session forks at most four distinct lookups at once. Missing apps and failed icon renders retry after a one-minute backoff. Shared work-log summaries mention repeated source names once. Existing stored fallback names are not backfilled; contracts are unchanged, and tool events carry app references rather than image bytes. ## Screenshots Matched fixtures showing Shottr's asset-catalog icon and two unavailable apps. **Before** ![Before: repeated Computer Use labels and generic Shottr icons](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/a272f9e2-190b-4491-8ba0-bf4cb1733983) **After** ![After: native app names and icons, with a single fallback label](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/c1eb8530-0b13-4cd7-a6ea-74cea289c02f) ## Validation - 223 focused tests pass across shared native icons, server asset access, Codex activity, work-log presentation, and SnapShots, including timeout, cache-recovery, slow-lookup warm-up, and in-flight lookup cap behavior. - Real macOS icon rendering verified at 64 and 128 pixels, including a visible-pixel check. - [Windows verification](https://github.com/SunkenInTime/t3code/actions/runs/34258855361) passes native lookup/rendering checks for executable paths, executable IDs, and a packaged Windows app, plus the shared resolver tests, without Electron. - CI typecheck, targeted lint, and format checks pass. - UI evidence covers Zen/Shottr computer use, Chrome browser use, failed-call icons, and duplicate fallback labels. Windows verification exercises native helpers; a Windows desktop GUI session and mobile were not separately launched. Model: GPT-6 Astra and Claude Fable 5.1. Harness: Codex and Claude Code. > [!NOTE] > ### Share native app icon resolution across tool activity and desktop snapshots > - Adds a shared `nativeAppIcon` package ([nativeAppIcon.ts](https://github.com/pingdotgg/t3code/pull/10626/files#diff-a7875b726742680f0300cab2a7b4ffeb98fb70ff3c61572c79a22f7b7c729325)) that resolves and renders native application icons on macOS and Windows, replacing the server-local implementation in [NativeAppIconResolver.ts](https://github.com/pingdotgg/t3code/pull/10626/files#diff-615008179672aa3821a4d570e0c63d6f9e369166fc977124777311f6b6ba131a). The resolver caches results with a 1-hour success TTL, 1-minute failure TTL, 256-entry capacity, and 2-permit concurrency limit. > - Updates [CodexAdapter.ts](https://github.com/pingdotgg/t3code/pull/10626/files#diff-f37bcac225467446dcf6198df38d357c15304b19eebacbdcdea70047f507707d) so computer-use events resolve native app display names and icons, with a 250-millisecond timeout that falls back to the original event metadata if the lookup is slow or fails. > - Updates [DesktopSnapShot.ts](https://github.com/pingdotgg/t3code/pull/10626/files#diff-f807f7d21590c2a67e4a431c25526d5631a5d0ebf3f2887e615559643fe3453b) to embed resolved native app icons as base64 PNG data URLs in snapshot metadata, falling back to the existing platform-specific icon lookup when native resolution is unavailable. > - Adds Windows PowerShell scripts in [windowsNativeApp.ts](https://github.com/pingdotgg/t3code/pull/10626/files#diff-7194be716db8548c56adaefaa43270cce82514f364c9836317299fb130613c80) for application metadata lookup and icon rendering, passing app references as structured data rather than command arguments to avoid shell injection. > - Deduplicates repeated source names in work-log summaries in [presentation.ts](https://github.com/pingdotgg/t3code/pull/10626/files#diff-b6852793cd3916fd7bb7704e9bfe1391f7ca44403063a0502eb92d59f5060972), using the count of distinct displayed names for singular/plural integration wording. > - Behavioral Change: the shared resolver renders icons at 64px for tool activity and 128px for desktop snapshots; failed or unsupported lookups return null and fall back to previous icon behavior. The Codex adapter now performs a bounded application lookup on every computer-use item lifecycle event, adding up to 250ms latency before fallback. > > > > Macroscope summarized 540cc85. > > ## Summary by CodeRabbit * **New Features** * Added cross-platform native application recognition and icon support for macOS and Windows. * Computer-use activity can display the identified application’s name and icon, including applications identified from tool arguments. * Desktop captures use native application icons when available, with a file-icon fallback. * Application icons support requested dimensions and cached reuse. * **Bug Fixes** * Failed lookups are retried after one minute without delaying activity updates beyond 250ms. * Prevented duplicate application names in work-log summaries and corrected singular/plural labeling.

records.title: fix(server): serialize checkpoint restores with pending turns
records.body:
## What Changed

Checkpoint restore now changes only paths owned by the selected checkpoints instead of broadly cleaning the worktree. Capture, restore, and provider-start work are serialized so a restore cannot race a later turn into the filesystem or provider history.

The same checkpoint boundary preserves every accepted queued message through concurrent and failed reverts. Pending and provider-submitted starts carry durable message/turn correlation through projection rebuilds, restart, steering, acknowledgement/runtime reordering, stale unrelated session events, and skewed client timestamps. Revert now deletes only concrete turns beyond its checkpoint boundary, leaving queued placeholder identities and their accepted order intact. A request-scoped rendezvous handles the narrow case where a provider lifecycle completes before its durable start acknowledgement; legacy event replay does not enroll or accumulate historical turns.

Provider-accepted starts now keep retrying their durable acknowledgement without sending the prompt again. Startup cleanup attempts every submitted entry even if one correlated failure activity cannot be persisted. If any entry fails, it keeps the session nonterminal so that entry remains retryable on the next restart; successfully persisted entries still clear independently. When cleanup succeeds, restart persists each correlated failure before making the session terminal, and server/client projections clear only that submitted identity.

This is one dependent checkpoint/revert correctness boundary despite the 35-file diff. The original scoped Git fix exposed loss windows in the event, SQL projection, reactor, startup reconciliation, and client read-model paths; splitting those layers would knowingly leave accepted work deletable, reorderable, or replayable between PRs. The independent restart snapshot query remains split into stacked PR #10611.

## Why

The Linux core nightly reproduced R08 deleting `unrelated.txt`, a user file outside the agent checkpoint. Focused red tests then reproduced checkpoint capture racing index restore, queued messages disappearing or changing order during revert, provider starts replaying after restart, stale terminal events clearing newer work, failed-turn files surviving restore, startup snapshot/subscription gaps, acknowledgement/runtime races permanently blocking later settle or revert commands, acknowledgement dispatch failing twice after one successful provider send, one failed startup cleanup preventing later submitted starts from clearing, and an acknowledged orphan remaining submitted after its session became terminal.

The repaired model quiesces checkpoint work before later provider starts, scopes Git restore to checkpoint-owned paths, and keeps request correlation state until the matching lifecycle or failure resolves it.

## Verification

At exact head `2193d32c2a19c051d12eaa30c951abe2da8b8cb9` rebased on upstream `7220dfe2c949476eaa7d21eccbcd3a0ce0eddb49`:

- 377/377 focused tests pass across 12 files, covering Git checkpoint restore, checkpoint/provider reactors, projection pipeline and replay, startup reconciliation, settle/revert admission, server/client projectors, imports, and contracts. The submission-rendezvous regression exhausts all 66 causally valid request A/B, acknowledgement A/B, running, and terminal orderings, asserting revert safety for every incomplete prefix and drained state after completion. Separate regressions cover reversed client clocks, two acknowledgement dispatch defects after one provider send, per-entry startup cleanup after an earlier persistence failure, correlated orphan cleanup in both live projectors, and reconstruction of submitted identity from a real persisted `projection_turns` row.
- Scoped lint exits 0. It reports eight pre-existing unused-parameter warnings in `ProviderCommandReactor.test.ts` and no errors.
- Formatting and the server, `@t3tools/client-runtime`, and `@t3tools/contracts` typechecks each exit 0; existing Effect typecheck suggestions remain non-errors.
- Direct Claude Opus 5 high review was attempted and exited 1 because its OAuth session expired. A fresh read-only Codex/Sol high review of the rebased exact head found no actionable issues, including at the sole rebase conflict where upstream question-attachment cleanup and this contribution's turn-correlation import were both retained.

The retained integration package at product head `0fcaff9445b5ca4ccaf4bef255419ec44e6f532d` passed the production Linux core suite 16/16 with current harness head `f9c916b1d596375eaee1669b49cbaa861da1b582` and qualified image digest `sha256:9510753c8e09ead6321ac91c71d13dbbf1163ebe4de909f9eb0786d3a9cd2e41`. That qualification ran with the actual scheduled unprivileged, read-only, 2 CPU, 4 GiB, 512 MiB `/dev/shm`, `/tmp` 2 GiB tmpfs, and `/desktop` 512 MiB tmpfs profile; Docker and the pinned verifier exited 0. This is intermediate product evidence—not proof for this PR head. The final exact-head multi-PR integration package, desktop artifact, and complete production receipt are missing, so this PR remains a draft.

This is a nonvisual filesystem/event-ordering repair. Screenshots and interaction video would not demonstrate the authoritative Git, persistence, or receipt boundaries and are not included.

records.title: fix(mcp): keep preview snapshots usable by the agent and let it save them
records.body:
## Problem Traced from thread `ed7dbe9f` (Bulk Project Selection in Onboarding). The agent used the collaborative browser to verify a UI change and then could not show the result. Three server-side causes: 1. **Every `preview_snapshot` result was truncated by the harness.** The tool's text content carried the full accessibility tree, 20 KB of visible text, and interactive elements whose `name` was the `innerText` of `[role]` containers. On the onboarding page three elements each carried the entire 20 KB project list. Claude Code caps MCP output at 25k tokens and replaces the whole result with a truncation notice, so the agent lost the locators along with everything else. Both snapshots in that thread hit this. 2. **`preview_evaluate` failed on any non-object result.** Effect's MCP server sets `structuredContent` to whatever the handler returns, and Claude Code rejects the call when that is an array or primitive. The agent's first `document.querySelectorAll(...).map(...)` call errored with "malformed result that failed schema validation" and it had to retry with `JSON.stringify`. 3. **There was no way to save the screenshot.** The PNG only existed inside the tool result. The agent guessed a path under the worktree, wrote nothing there, and the chat rendered "Image unavailable". ## Fix - `preview_snapshot` text is bounded under 60 KB: drop the accessibility tree, cap visible text at 8k chars and element names at 200, keep the newest 40 log entries, and halve interactive elements only as a last resort. A second text block tells the agent what was cut. `structuredContent` is unchanged. - The desktop snapshot script caps element names at 200 chars at the source, so remote and web hosts send less over the wire too. - `preview_evaluate` returns `{ value }` so `structuredContent` is always an object. - `preview_snapshot` accepts `save: true`, writes the PNG to `/browser-artifacts` (same directory the desktop uses for recordings), and returns `screenshotPath`. The tool description tells the agent to embed it as `![alt](screenshotPath)`. - Snapshot failure text now names the error tag. Not fixed here: the thread's worktree did not get `vp i` from the setup script because the `t3code-3` project has no scripts configured in T3 Code (the `t3.json` setup script is only offered for import). That is a config gap on this machine, not a code bug. Overlaps with #9261 (save) and #9505 (bounding); this PR covers both root causes from one real failure plus the evaluate fix. Closes #7410 ## Closes discussions - https://github.com/pingdotgg/t3code/discussions/9200 ## Verification `vp test run apps/server/src/mcp apps/desktop/src/preview/Manager.test.ts apps/desktop/src/ipc/methods/preview.test.ts` (140 tests), targeted lint and typecheck for server and desktop. Written by Claude Fable 5.1 through Claude Code in T3 Code. 🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code) > [!NOTE] > ### Bound `preview_snapshot` agent-visible text and add server-side screenshot saving > - `preview_snapshot` text content is now bounded: `visibleText` truncated to 8,000 chars, interactive element names to 200 chars, `accessibilityTree` omitted, and console/network/action arrays capped to newest 40 entries. A second text content item lists omitted fields. > - Added an optional `save` boolean to the `preview_snapshot` input schema. When true, the server writes the decoded PNG to `ServerConfig.browserArtifactsDir` and returns `screenshotPath`; the `save` flag is stripped before the request reaches the browser. > - `preview_evaluate` results are now wrapped as `{ value: result }` with a typed output schema instead of returning an arbitrary JSON value. > - Failed `preview_snapshot` calls now include the derived error tag (e.g. `PreviewAutomationExecutionError`, `PreviewScreenshotSaveError`) in the text response. > - Behavioral Change: `preview_evaluate` consumers must read `result.value` instead of the top-level result; `preview_snapshot` text content no longer includes `accessibilityTree` and may contain a second text content item with omission notices. Screenshot save failures map to `PreviewScreenshotSaveError`. > > > >
> 📊 Macroscope summarized 7a64017. 5 files reviewed, 3 issues evaluated, 0 issues filtered, 2 comments posted > > ### 🗂️ Filtered Issues > >
> ## Summary by CodeRabbit * **New Features** * Preview snapshots can save screenshots and return their file paths for reuse. * Preview evaluation results now use a consistent `{value}` format. * **Bug Fixes** * Snapshot output is bounded to prevent oversized responses, with notes indicating omitted or shortened content. * Interactive element names and visible text are truncated when necessary. * Snapshot failures now provide clearer error details. * Saved screenshot failures are reported explicitly.

records.title: fix(server): recover checkpoint revert sessions after restart
records.body: Checkpoint revert fails after a server restart because it requires a live provider session before reaching the existing session recovery path. Prepare the rollback by checking provider support and recovering the persisted session before reading its working directory or changing files. Unsupported providers are rejected before recovery; a recovery failure preserves files, checkpoint refs, and history. Failed recovery attempts stop their provider session and revoke and clear MCP credentials, including when binding persistence or provider validation fails. The service method and its test doubles are renamed to describe rollback preparation. Fixes #10470. Validation: 128 tests passed across the provider, checkpoint reactor, and orchestration integration suites, with one existing skip. Server typecheck, formatting, and focused lint passed. Two preparation regressions fail against the old service behavior and pass with the fix. Coverage includes inactive Codex/Claude sessions, turn-zero revert, recovery failure, failed-recovery cleanup including a stop error, and persisted routing across a service restart. Native provider CLIs and the reported Windows installation were not exercised. Model: GPT-6. Harness: Codex in T3 Code. > [!NOTE] > ### Recover persisted provider sessions before checkpoint revert in `CheckpointReactor` > - Renames the `ProviderService` rollback-support assertion method to `prepareConversationRollback` and makes it resume inactive persisted sessions after capability validation but before any file or workspace changes. > - The `CheckpointReactor` revert handler removes the initial active-session and Git-repository checks and now calls `prepareConversationRollback` before resolving the session runtime and restoring workspace state. > - Failed persisted-session recovery now attempts to stop the partially recovered provider session and revoke its MCP credential, using the configured revocation callback instead of the module-global registry function. > - Risk: `ProviderService.cleanup` now relies on `ProviderServiceLiveOptions.mcpRevoke` being set; if callers construct the layer without the revocation hook, MCP credential cleanup will be skipped during recovery failures. > > > > Macroscope summarized b988ee3. > > ## Summary by CodeRabbit * **Bug Fixes** * Improved conversation rollback by recovering inactive provider sessions before reverting changes. * Prevented partially recovered sessions from leaving behind active processes or MCP credentials when recovery fails. * Improved rollback validation and error reporting when persisted provider session information is unavailable. * Ensured rollback behavior remains consistent across supported provider sessions and recovery scenarios.

records.title: [Bug]: Checkpoint revert fails with "No active provider session with workspace cwd is bound to this thread" even when session projection is ready
records.body:
## Before submitting

- [x] I searched existing issues and did not find a duplicate.
- [x] I included enough detail to reproduce or investigate the problem.

## Area

apps/server (checkpoint revert / provider session binding)

## Steps to reproduce

1. Have a thread with several completed turns using the Claude Agent provider (`claudeAgent`), no isolated worktree (repo opened directly, `worktree_path` is null for the thread in `state.sqlite`).
2. Let the app/server go through a restart (in this case: an auto-update from an older nightly to `0.0.38`).
3. Immediately after the new server comes up, open the thread and use checkpoint revert to roll back to an earlier turn (turn 9 in this case).
4. Retry the revert.

## Expected behavior

Checkpoint revert either succeeds, or transparently re-establishes a provider session bound to the thread's workspace cwd before attempting the revert, the way a new chat message does.

## Actual behavior

Checkpoint revert fails immediately, every time, with:

```json
{"turnCount":9,"detail":"No active provider session with workspace cwd is bound to this thread."}
```

Confirmed via `projection_thread_activities` in `state.sqlite`: 8 consecutive `checkpoint.revert.failed` events for the same thread between `2026-09-07T02:45:16Z` and `2026-09-07T03:11:23Z` — the last one just 38 seconds after the new server process started (`server-runtime.json` → `startedAt: 2026-09-07T03:10:45.871Z`). Same failure also occurred once earlier, on `2026-08-28`.

At the time of failure, `projection_thread_sessions` for the thread already reports `status = ready`, `provider_name = claudeAgent`, `active_turn_id = NULL` — i.e. the projection looks healthy, but checkpoint revert still can't find a live provider process to bind to the workspace cwd. This looks related to the provider-session/projection reconciliation work in #4584, #7719, and #7463, but those are about turns getting stuck on `Working` after a crash/restart — this is a *different* trigger: the session projection is already settled (`ready`), yet the specific checkpoint-revert path still can't obtain a bound session.

Sending a plain chat message to the same thread (starting a fresh turn) is *not* something I've verified recovers it yet — flagging that as untested, not a confirmed workaround.

## Impact

Minor degradation — blocks checkpoint revert on the affected thread; other thread actions (new messages) appear unaffected.

## Version or commit

T3 Code (Alpha) 0.0.38 (Windows, desktop installer)

## Environment

Windows 11 Pro (10.0.26200), desktop app, Claude Agent provider

## Logs or stack traces

```
state.sqlite / projection_thread_activities:
  kind = 'checkpoint.revert.failed'
  payload_json = '{"turnCount":9,"detail":"No active provider session with workspace cwd is bound to this thread."}'
  created_at: 2026-09-07T02:45:16.143Z, 02:45:51.003Z, 02:46:25.889Z, 02:57:00.328Z,
              02:58:31.836Z, 02:58:36.256Z, 03:11:14.390Z, 03:11:23.317Z
  (earlier occurrence: 2026-08-28T11:59:33.440Z, 11:59:41.144Z)

server-runtime.json:
  {"pid":28088,"host":"127.0.0.1","port":3773,"startedAt":"2026-09-07T03:10:45.871Z"}

projection_thread_sessions (at time of last failure):
  status = ready, provider_name = claudeAgent, active_turn_id = NULL
```

records.title: fix(server): capture checkpoints before refreshing PR status
records.body: CheckpointReactor ran the git status refresh on the same worker as checkpoint capture, and before it. That refresh ends in a remote PR lookup under the vcs status write lock. A fast follow-up message could edit files before the capture committed, so the checkpoint recorded the wrong tree. The refresh now runs on its own drainable worker (`statusRefreshWorker`). Turn completion enqueues the refresh and moves straight to capture, so capture never waits behind the network call and checkpoints for other threads do not queue behind it either. `drain` waits on both workers. One test pins the behavior: the PR refresh blocks on a Deferred that stays open until the `checkpoint.diff.finalized` receipt lands and the ref contains the edited file. Extracted from #10297. Written by Claude Fable 5.1 in Claude Code. > [!NOTE] > ### Decouple local git status refresh from checkpoint capture in `CheckpointReactor` > - Completion events in [CheckpointReactor.ts](https://github.com/pingdotgg/t3code/pull/10347/files#diff-79dc41615f79575ae1404bd102df915797fb24ba34989557f80e229d305521fb) now enqueue status refresh work on a separate drainable worker instead of awaiting it inline, so checkpoint processing can proceed while the refresh is pending > - The reactor drain operation now waits for both the main worker and the new status-refresh worker > - Non-interruption failures in the status-refresh worker are logged and swallowed; only interruption causes propagate > - Adds test coverage in [CheckpointReactor.test.ts](https://github.com/pingdotgg/t3code/pull/10347/files#diff-80f47e48c3258a501e94a5ba8b5ee0e8871faf64acfe837965b6ca6caf324279) for capturing a turn's checkpoint while pull-request status lookup is still pending > - Behavioral Change: `CheckpointReactor.make` drain now blocks on queued status refreshes; callers relying on drain completing without pending refresh work will see different timing > > > > Macroscope summarized 5d98a6c. > >

records.title: fix(orchestration): preserve conversation order across clock rollback
records.body: ## What Changed Conversation items now keep their first persisted event sequence through streaming updates, snapshot reloads, and replay. Web, desktop, and mobile use that key to order messages, plans, and work-log entries, independently of host timestamps and provider-local sequence counters. Migration 048 backfills keys from retained events without rewriting timestamps or payloads. Turn pagination uses the initiating prompt's key, preserves legacy cursors, and keeps indexed range reads. Revert retains the correct prompt-and-answer pair after a clock correction. Backward terminal timestamps render as `Worked` without inventing an elapsed duration. ## Why When the host clock moves backward during a turn, timestamp sorting can place an answer before its prompt and newer tasks before older ones. Reloading or paging preserves the wrong order, and reverting can retain a newer prompt with an older answer. Fixes #9772 ### Proposal Use persisted event order as the conversation's ordering key, keep timestamps for display, and anchor each paginated turn to its initiating prompt. Backfill retained history and preserve compatibility with older snapshots and cursors. ## Testing - 625 focused tests pass across 17 suites covering contracts, migration, persistence, projection/replay, paging, web/mobile work logs, optimistic sends, and shared client state. - Review regressions cover incoming events during send preparation, delayed checkpoints during a running turn with a queued prompt, and query-specific legacy cursor decode errors. - The focused HTTP/WebSocket transfer-budget test passes. The snapshot cap allows 650 additional bytes for creation keys, measured at 612/616 compressed bytes for the Codex/Claude fixtures; total-transfer and WebSocket caps are unchanged. - The revert regression fails on upstream `4f782beda`, retaining `new-prompt` with `assistant-1`; the branch retains `old-prompt` with `assistant-1`. - Targeted server, web, mobile, client-runtime, contracts, and shared package typechecks pass. Existing Effect suggestions remain outside this change. - Focused lint and formatting pass. Existing ChatView lint warnings remain outside the changed logic. - SQLite query-plan assertions verify indexed sequence-range pagination, including hydration queries. - Isolated browser verification compares the upstream baseline and this branch using equivalent synthetic projection fixtures with an 11-hour rollback. Reload and work-log expansion preserve the corrected order. These visual fixtures are not a substitute for the persistence/replay tests above. - The fixtures do not run a provider turn or change the host clock. Native mobile, real provider sessions, and relay mode were not exercised in the browser pass. ### Before The original Task 1 prompt appears after Task 2 and both answers. ![Upstream places Task 1's prompt after both answers](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/9d506001-5503-46ab-a3ed-f2167bcb216a) ### After Each prompt stays before its work and answer, including after reload. The first turn crosses the clock correction, so its elapsed duration is unknown. ![The fix keeps both tasks in persisted event order](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/96aebd78-a28b-4205-b06a-7fe3783b0dc7) ### Interaction recording Loading the saved thread and expanding both work logs in a 1280×800 Chromium client. The initial before/after pass used the app browser over Tailscale; this recording repeats the interaction locally for upload, with no page errors. https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/01928aa6-d889-4360-9ab3-e7b6a47f2f51 ## Checklist - [x] One concern: preserve conversation order across host clock corrections - [x] Explained what changed and why - [x] Added regression tests and migration coverage - [x] Included before/after screenshots - [x] Included an interaction recording Model: GPT-6 Astra Harness: T3 code > [!NOTE] > ### Preserve conversation order across clock rollback with `createdSequence` > - Adds a persisted `createdSequence` column to projected messages, proposed plans, activities, and turns, populated from the originating event sequence and preserved across updates > - Replaces timestamp-first ordering with creation-sequence-first ordering across projection reads, snapshot queries, keyset cursors, thread reducers, and client timeline derivation > - Adds migration 48 to backfill `created_sequence` from thread event history and recompute summary fields (latest user message, pending input count, actionable plan) > - Updates `threadDetailCursor` to version 2 with sequence boundaries, translating legacy cursors via a SQL lookup > - Adds shared `compareCreatedOrder` and `nextLocalMessageSequence` helpers in `packages/shared/src/chronology.ts`, used by server, web, and mobile ordering logic > - Risk: migration 48 backfills four projection tables from event history; rows without a matching event (orphans or prior thread incarnations) receive no sequence and sort as legacy zero — verify [048_ProjectionThreadCreatedSequence.ts](https://github.com/pingdotgg/t3code/pull/10325/files#diff-52f5ee925451848aca6f5328310553317adef42525f543f0a618bae9d615da93) event-matching bounds and the `thread.created` upper limit > > > > Macroscope summarized dec6232. > >

records.title: fix(server): recover interrupted checkpoint rewinds
records.body: A failed rewind can leave files, the provider conversation, and T3 history at different checkpoints. Retrying a relative provider rollback can remove more history. Save each rewind step before moving on. Retry the same checkpoint to finish after a failure or restart. Keep a safety Git ref until the history commit succeeds, and block new thread operations while recovery is pending. Codex forks at the saved checkpoint turn ID without changing or resuming the source conversation. It preserves active goals without running them. Missing native IDs stop the rewind before files change. This requires Codex 0.153.0 or later. OpenCode rewind is temporarily blocked because saved checkpoints do not identify its exact native conversation boundary. Safe rewind is unavailable for Claude, Cursor, Grok, and Antigravity because their adapters cannot preserve the required native history. Stacked on [#10294](https://github.com/pingdotgg/t3code/pull/10294) for typed lifecycle completion and the earlier server fixes. The parent includes migration 48. This PR adds migration 49. Git ref cleanup is best effort. A crash after the durable restore commit can retain obsolete refs. User files and the provider conversation are already consistent. ## Verification - 172 focused tests passed. Covers failure after file restore, cursor adoption, restart recovery, exact native boundaries, and blocked commands. - 17 integration tests passed. One existing test is skipped. - After review fixes, 132 focused and integration tests passed, with one existing skip. This includes reactor restart recovery and bounded provider errors. - Restacked onto the final lifecycle parent. All 11 rewind commits are unchanged. The restack passed 224 focused and integration tests, then 150 tests after the parent request-correlation fix. Each run had one existing skip. - Server typecheck and targeted lint passed. Lint has eight existing unused-parameter warnings. - Disposable native Codex 0.153.4 check passed. Partial and empty forks kept an active goal with no model requests or source/config changes. ## Client check A synthetic browser session switched from Codex to OpenCode using capability data from a disposable local server. The Codex rewind control is enabled. The OpenCode action is absent. No rewind command or provider session ran during this check. The native Codex fixture above is separate proof. | Codex | OpenCode | | --- | --- | | ![Codex rewind control enabled](https://files.tslop.org/2026/09/rewind-codex-control-6e63bd69.png) | ![OpenCode rewind action absent](https://files.tslop.org/2026/09/rewind-opencode-blocked-4e2c4db1.png) | Created with Codex. Closes #8958 > [!NOTE] > ### Recover interrupted checkpoint reverts with staged, persistent rollback attempts > - Checkpoint reverts now execute as resumable staged attempts persisted in `checkpoint_revert_attempts`; failures after file or conversation mutation retain the attempt and emit a recovery-required activity instead of a terminal failure > - Conversation rollback moves from a single-step call to a three-stage `prepareConversationRollback` / `forkConversation` / `rollbackConversation` flow across [ProviderService.ts](https://github.com/pingdotgg/t3code/pull/10299/files#diff-b9b9384b78856ff56cff5dd0ccb106054fb5d2d1b7500fcd30d8938ebfec5775), with Codex adapter support added in [CodexConversationRollback.ts](https://github.com/pingdotgg/t3code/pull/10299/files#diff-37fe083ca13bbd35e359591f26d1b805a1427deadb1f2e4cbc0bd2836d6240d2) > - `OrchestrationEngine` rejects conflicting thread mutations while a revert is unfinished, reserving revert state before command acknowledgment > - `TurnCheckpointCapture` coordinates provider turn termination with checkpoint file capture, blocking subsequent turns until the prior capture completes > - Orchestration projections now carry typed pending-operation state (turn vs compact) across the full lifecycle; shared `derivePendingRequests` consolidates approval and user-input derivation from web and mobile into [pendingRequests.ts](https://github.com/pingdotgg/t3code/pull/10299/files#diff-301834b20cf74929c3fffdc40f7da55f6c4b3f083dfa07f4956b084bce79ea1e) > - Risk: rollback API is a breaking change — callers must use `prepareConversationRollback` + `forkConversation` + `rollbackConversation` instead of the removed single-step method; migration 049 adds the `checkpoint_revert_attempts` table; older snapshots without `pendingOperation` fields fall back to legacy timestamp-based matching > > > > Macroscope summarized 9e29383. > >

records.title: fix(server): wait for terminal checkpoints before new messages
records.body: A follow-up message can edit files before the previous turn's checkpoint captures them. Slow pull request lookups can extend that window. Track terminal events before logging or runtime consumers receive them. The application owns one capture service shared by the provider and both reactors. Hold new messages for that thread until capture succeeds, skips, or fails. Reserve the known active turn before an interrupt returns. Keep git status and pull request refresh work outside the capture worker. Active-turn steering still goes through. A second stop cancels messages waiting for capture. Capture failures and non-git projects do not block the next message. Verified after restacking with 195 focused server tests, the server typecheck, and targeted lint. The two new ordering tests fail on current main because the next turn edits files before capture. One existing real-Codex test requires a local binary and was skipped. This covers known terminal events and explicit interrupt ordering. It does not make native turn admission atomic with terminal events that arrive during send preparation, or change ambiguous interrupt error recovery. Stacked on [#10120](https://github.com/pingdotgg/t3code/pull/10120) to keep the related server changes in merge order. Created with Codex. Updated with Codex. > [!NOTE] > ### Wait for terminal checkpoint capture before starting next provider message > - Adds `TurnCheckpointCapture` service in [TurnCheckpointCapture.ts](https://github.com/pingdotgg/t3code/pull/10297/files#diff-3f3c85190d213b207bc99f3fcfecca6c20fb7f57e2ac9909021a9ae1fac3b2ee) to track per-thread pending captures for terminal provider events (completed/aborted) and interrupt reservations > - `ProviderService.publishRuntimeEvent` in [ProviderService.ts](https://github.com/pingdotgg/t3code/pull/10297/files#diff-b9b9384b78856ff56cff5dd0ccb106054fb5d2d1b7500fcd30d8938ebfec5775) now observes events through `TurnCheckpointCapture` before canonical logging and PubSub publication; `interruptTurn` and `stopSession` register interrupt expectations before adapter calls > - `ProviderCommandReactor` in [ProviderCommandReactor.ts](https://github.com/pingdotgg/t3code/pull/10297/files#diff-0630e9ad70d5dcd1c8586d29297f9b7d5f5436cc8e10fc88dc22acc511f1450d) holds turn-start requests for a thread with pending checkpoint capture and resumes them via internal `capture-ready` inputs once the capture completes; cancellation commands remove delayed requests and still invoke the provider interrupt or stop > - `CheckpointReactor` in [CheckpointReactor.ts](https://github.com/pingdotgg/t3code/pull/10297/files#diff-79dc41615f79575ae1404bd102df915797fb24ba34989557f80e229d305521fb) delegates completed/aborted event handling to `processTurnCompletion`, which signals `TurnCheckpointCapture.complete` on exit and moves Git status refresh to a separate drainable worker > - Behavioral Change: `ProviderService` construction now requires `TurnCheckpointCapture`; `RuntimeCoreDependenciesLive` in [server.ts](https://github.com/pingdotgg/t3code/pull/10297/files#diff-a8f34e8f17024480f0ca046c8ea4a8af3b525fe68940b703ba496fa4aa4ddfbd) provides it, and all test layers updated to include it > > > > Macroscope summarized 42e41b3. > >

records.title: fix(mcp): allow text-only preview snapshots
records.body: Closes #10187. Repeated `preview_snapshot` calls add a PNG to each MCP result. Providers or gateways with image-count limits may reject the accumulated conversation. Add optional `includeImage`. `{"includeImage":false}` returns fresh page metadata and JSON text without an image content part. Omitted or `true` preserves the existing PNG response. The flag stays inside the MCP server. Browser capture and the shared snapshot contract are unchanged. The user selected this opt-in mitigation with current defaults preserved. It cannot remove images already in provider-owned history, does not stop host capture, and does not guarantee that a gateway accepts an existing conversation. The reporter's original gateway rejection was not replayed. Verification on integrated main [585ce2c2](https://github.com/pingdotgg/t3code/commit/585ce2c2ab396e4c3c5ffcfc422449c07896ddf9): - The registered MCP tool and real preview broker use a synthetic host. Exact-main before controls fail twice and pass 12 tests. The candidate passes all 14, including the existing HTTP session lifecycle test. - Six text-only calls return fresh metadata with no image. A following default call returns PNG again. Repeated default and explicit-image calls preserve the PNG bytes and metadata. Tab targeting, bounded host errors and invalid inputs are covered. - The orchestrator independently reviewed all four changed files, ran both sides, and passed scoped typecheck and changed-file lint. Two unchanged Effect suggestions remain in the server environment machine. The subsequent [f12d3935](https://github.com/pingdotgg/t3code/commit/f12d39359f0f76a64ff2d77959c5baf821df15be) main update does not change the MCP implementation or preview contracts. No client UI changed, so screenshots are not applicable. This is protocol/output evidence, not a browser, native or real-provider claim. Ready for human review; unmerged. Current-head CI finished with 16 successful and four skipped checks. The orchestrator read all check outputs, annotations, comments and reviews; no unresolved finding remains. The configured Cursor review is paused by its spending limit, so its successful dispatch is not claimed as a code review. Implemented with GPT 6 Astra via Codex in T3 Code. > [!NOTE] > ### Allow text-only preview snapshots in `McpHttpServer` > - Adds test coverage for `includeImage=false` and omitted `includeImage` in `preview_snapshot`, verifying failure responses stay bounded and omit image content > - Adds a parameterized integration test confirming repeated `preview_snapshot` calls return fresh metadata with distinct titles, include a PNG by default or when explicitly enabled, and omit it when disabled > - Adds rejection tests for non-boolean `includeImage` values (string, numeric, null), asserting they fail with an `AiError` summary before browser-host selection > - Risk: no behavioral change beyond test coverage; all modifications are in [McpHttpServer.test.ts](https://github.com/pingdotgg/t3code/pull/10232/files#diff-552121f7256046a957f60f7f3476debc694a83547a2f5f9874be39fe468aa5f6) > > > > Macroscope summarized 3d458d3. > >

records.title: feat: add thread provenance and selective agent rollback
records.body: ## What Changed - Records each completed agent turn as a file-level change set using T3 Code's existing checkpoint refs and durable activity stream. - Adds a Provenance panel for reviewing changed files, the producing turn, provider, and recorded line ranges. - Previews and applies selective code undo for one turn while preserving compatible work added afterward. - Surfaces shared-checkout overlap, unattributed dirty-file changes, worktree mismatch, and recovery failures above the composer. - Opens the relevant checkpoint diff and conversation directly from provenance controls. - Adds integration guidance for deciding which parallel turns can combine independently and which require review. ## Why A full checkpoint rewind can erase valid work that happened after one bad agent turn. Provenance lets users identify the responsible turn, inspect its checkpoint patch, and remove only that turn when Git proves the reverse patch still applies cleanly. ## Safety Details - Provenance is opt-in with `T3_PROVENANCE_ENABLED=1` while the workflow is evaluated. - Selective undo derives a context-anchored patch from the target turn's before and after checkpoint refs, preventing stale offsets or duplicate lines from being reversed accidentally. - Git checks the complete reverse patch against the live workspace before applying it. A conflicting multi-file patch is refused without partially modifying files. - Binary changes and renames remain review-only. - Later compatible edits and conversation history remain intact; nearby ambiguous edits are conservatively sent to manual review. - Successful undo writes a durable receipt containing the affected paths and patch SHA-256. - Turn summaries reuse the provider's existing final response. Provenance makes no additional model calls and adds no system-prompt content or provider tokens. ## Demo https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/1017acee-abc9-4c90-9fa9-831013b189eb ## UI ### Safe Undo attached to the composer ### Expanded recovery scope and turn provenance ## Testing 1. Start T3 Code with `T3_PROVENANCE_ENABLED=1`. 2. Run one turn that changes two files. 3. Run a later turn that changes a separate region in one of those files. 4. Open **Provenance**, select the earlier turn, and preview recovery. 5. Confirm the target patch is marked for removal and the compatible later change is preserved. 6. Apply the undo, then inspect the workspace diff and durable recovery receipt. 7. Modify the same target lines and retry; confirm the undo is refused and no file is partially changed. ## Verification - `vp run --filter @t3tools/client-runtime typecheck` - `vp run --filter t3 typecheck` - `vp run --filter @t3tools/web typecheck` - `node scripts/provenance-smoke-test.mjs` - `node --test scripts/provenance-undo.test.mjs` (8 real-Git recovery scenarios) - Focused checkpoint regression: exact 25,000-line provenance summaries - `git diff --check` - Manual validation covered attribution, conversation navigation, overlap alerts, recovery preview, prior-turn selection, and selective undo. ## Checklist - [x] Reuses T3 Code's checkpoint and activity architecture - [x] Makes no additional provider calls or prompt changes - [x] Refuses unsupported or conflicting recovery patches - [x] Preserves compatible later work in the Git-backed smoke test - [x] Includes one demo and two focused UI screenshots - [x] Documents the opt-in rollout flag Generated with GPT-5 and GPT-6 in OpenAI Codex desktop using the Codex harness. > [!NOTE] > ### Add thread provenance tracking and selective agent rollback > - Records per-file mutations, line ranges, and historical overlaps in `CheckpointReactor` to track agent changes. > - Adds `SafeHistoryPanel` and `SafeIntegrationPanel` to search, review, and classify turn changes by safe-undo readiness. > - Introduces UI banners, turn review cards, and a conflict review layout for provenance overlaps and workspace mismatches. > - Implements selective undo via reverse-patch validation and a new `provenance-turn` scope in the checkpoint revert command schema. > - Behavioral Change: Provenance is disabled by default and requires `T3_PROVENANCE_ENABLED=1`. Provider turns are now blocked before execution if the thread workspace path differs from the provider session cwd. > > > > Macroscope summarized 1e201e3. > >

records.title: [Bug]: Mobile thread stuck on "Loading messages..." forever when the snapshot fails schema decoding
records.body:
### Before submitting

- [x] I searched existing issues and did not find a duplicate.
- [x] I included enough detail to reproduce or investigate the problem.

### Area

apps/mobile (root cause in packages/client-runtime, so web connected to a mismatched remote is exposed too)

### Summary

Some threads never finish loading on the mobile app. The feed stays empty and the floating pill reads "Loading messages..." indefinitely. Nothing recovers it: force quit, relaunch, switching between T3 Connect and local network, or waiting. Other threads on the same server load normally. Desktop on the same machine as the server is fine.

Root cause: when a thread detail snapshot fails **schema decoding** on the client, both load paths swallow the failure and nothing retries or surfaces an error. The thread state stays `synchronizing` with no data and no error forever.

### Steps to reproduce

Real-world repro (observed):

1. Connect the mobile app to a T3 server on another machine over T3 Connect.
2. Open a thread whose detail snapshot contains something the phone's contracts reject (see "Likely trigger"). Never-opened threads only; a cached thread renders from cache with "Syncing".
3. Observe the empty feed and a permanent "Loading messages..." pill. Kill and relaunch; same result.

Deterministic harness repro (used to confirm the mechanism, using the harness from `packages/client-runtime/src/state/threads-atoms.test.ts`):

1. `ThreadSnapshotLoader.load` returns `Option.none()` (what the real loader does for every failure, including decode errors).
2. The `orchestration.subscribeThread` stream fails with `RpcClientError({ reason: RpcClientDefect })`, or dies with a defect (what the effect RPC client emits when a stream chunk fails `decodeChunk`; it uses `Effect.orDie`).
3. Mount `createEnvironmentThreadDetailAtoms(...).stateAtom(ref)` and wait.

Result: status `synchronizing`, `data: none`, `error: none`, exactly one subscribe attempt, no retry. Both the `RpcClientError` and defect variants behave the same.

### Expected behavior

The thread shows a "Could not load conversation" state with the decode error, or at minimum an error the user can act on. A decode failure should never be indistinguishable from a slow load.

### Actual behavior

Empty feed and "Loading messages..." forever. No error is surfaced anywhere in the UI. The only trace is a client-side `logWarning` ("Could not load the thread snapshot over HTTP; using the socket snapshot instead.").

### Diagnosis

Two swallow points in `packages/client-runtime`:

1. **HTTP path.** `threadSnapshotLoaderLayer` in `src/state/threadSnapshotHttp.ts` (`Effect.catchCause` around line 122) maps every failure, including `SchemaError` from the response decode, to `Option.none()` so the socket fallback can run. That is fine for network errors but hides schema failures, which the socket fallback cannot fix.
2. **Socket fallback.** The server re-sends the snapshot as the first stream chunk. The RPC client dies on chunk decode (`RpcClient.ts` `decodeChunk` + `Effect.orDie`). In `src/rpc/client.ts` (`subscribeDynamicMapped`, around line 232), `subscribeDynamic` classifies any `RpcClientError` as "Durable RPC subscription lost its transport; waiting for the next session" and drains the stream. The session is healthy, so no next session ever arrives. A pure defect skips `onExpectedFailure` and fails the forked fiber silently instead. Either way `setStreamError` is never called.

The state machine in `src/state/threads.ts` therefore never leaves `synchronizing`. On mobile, `ThreadDetailScreen` renders `contentPresentation: loading` plus the "Loading messages..." pill for that state, and `useEnvironmentThread` would also mask an atom failure by falling back to `EMPTY_ENVIRONMENT_THREAD_STATE`.

Why the desktop is unaffected: the bundled server and client are always the same build. The mismatch only appears when a client talks to a server built from a different commit, which is exactly the T3 Connect / mobile case (and hosted web against an older self-hosted server).

### Likely trigger

Not confirmed without the phone console log. The shell snapshot for the same threads decodes fine, so the offending field is detail-only (messages, activities, checkpoints, session). Strongest candidate: **file attachments**. #8235 (2026-08-28) added `type: "file"` attachments plus the `ChatUnknownAttachment` catch-all. A phone bundle built before that only knows `ChatAttachment = Union([ChatImageAttachment])`, so any thread that ever received a PDF/ZIP attachment fails to decode. Production/preview use fingerprint runtime versions, so a stale JS bundle on a phone is plausible.

Confirm by checking whether the stuck threads carry a file attachment, or by grabbing the console line starting `Could not load the thread snapshot over HTTP`; its cause names the failing path.

### Ruled out

- Server and relay: mobile relay HTTP and WebSocket sessions to a same-build server work normally in server traces.
- Snapshot size / decode speed: windowed (10 turn) snapshots from a real database are all under 500 KB and decode in ~1 ms on V8.
- Atom lifecycle after #9740 / #9913: render-before-subscribe and unmount-before-snapshot both recover in harness tests.

### Suggested fix

- In `subscribeDynamic`, treat `RpcClientError` with a `RpcClientDefect` reason (and defects) as terminal expected failures routed to `onExpectedFailure`, not as transport loss. Only socket/transport reasons should wait for the next session.
- In `threadSnapshotLoaderLayer`, surface decode failures (or at least distinguish them from network failures) instead of folding them into `Option.none()`; the socket fallback cannot recover a schema mismatch and just doubles the payload.
- Optionally show the incompatibility in the thread's unavailable state so users know to update the app or server.

### Impact

Major degradation: affected threads are unreachable from mobile with no feedback.

### Version or commit

main @ a324cabc0 (client-runtime code path). Server on the remote machine: unknown version. Phone: iOS TestFlight build (UA `T3Code/26`), version unknown.

### Environment

iOS, T3 Connect to a server on another machine; also reproduces on local network per user report.

### Workaround

None found. Threads without the offending content load normally.

records.title: preview_snapshot accumulates unbounded image attachments, breaking providers with per-request image limits
records.body:
**What happened**
While debugging an issue via the opencode provider (Kimi K3, routed through an internal AI Gateway), with T3 controlling/observing a browser preview against Storybook, the session died with: `Bad Request: {"error":"Upstream error: INVALID_ARGUMENT: parameter \"messages\" supports at most 5 images; received 6"}`. It happened twice in a row within the same investigation session.

**Diagnosis**
Every `preview_snapshot` tool call attaches a new screenshot (`image/png`) to the conversation, and nothing prunes older screenshot attachments from history before the next provider request. Confirmed in the provider event log: two separate opencode sub-sessions in the same thread each failed once enough `preview_snapshot` calls had accumulated (5+ completions per sub-session), each time with the identical "5 images / received 6" 400 from the upstream gateway. The gateway in this case enforces a hard per-request image cap of 5; opencode has no way to know that cap for a custom/generic OpenAI-compatible provider, and T3's `preview_snapshot` handler (`apps/server/src/mcp/toolkits/preview/handlers.ts`) does not bound how many prior screenshots stay live in context.

This is the same shape of problem as #7410 (unbounded `preview_snapshot` metadata exhausting context), fixed in #9505 by bounding output "at the MCP response boundary... so every provider is covered" — the same approach (cap the number of *live* image attachments carried forward from recent `preview_snapshot` calls, replacing older ones with a placeholder) would fix this for every provider, not just this one gateway.

**Steps to reproduce**
1. Configure an opencode provider pointed at a custom OpenAI-compatible endpoint that enforces a per-request image limit (e.g. 5).
2. Start a thread with the preview MCP toolkit enabled.
3. Have the agent call `preview_snapshot` repeatedly (e.g. iterating on a browser/Storybook page) more times than the endpoint's image limit, in the same thread, without the images being pruned from history.
4. The next turn's request exceeds the provider's image limit and the whole turn fails with an unrecoverable 400.

**Version**
0.0.39-nightly.20260905.1289 (commit `8d3c56b487810455f7b695d1b849b4370b132d03`)

**Environment**
macOS 15.6 (darwin arm64), Node v24.19.0, T3 Code nightly desktop app; opencode provider (`@opencode-ai/sdk` ^1.3.15) against a custom OpenAI-compatible AI gateway serving two internally-routed model deployments (a Kimi K3 deployment and a GLM-5.3-flash deployment).

**Evidence**
"error":{"name":"APIError","data":{"message":"Bad Request: {"error":"Upstream error: INVALID_ARGUMENT: parameter \"messages\" supports at most 5 images; received 6"}","statusCode":400,"isRetryable":false,"metadata":{"url":"https://<internal-ai-gateway>/ai-gateway/mlflow/v1/chat/completions"}}}
(Two occurrences, ~11 minutes apart, same thread, different opencode sub-sessions, different underlying model deployment each time.)

**Related issues**
#7410 / #9505 — same root cause category (`preview_snapshot` context bloat), but that fix bounds JSON *metadata* size, not the *count* of image attachments, so it would not have prevented this. Not a duplicate.

**Fix applied or workaround**
None applied to the install. User advised to avoid long single threads with heavy `preview_snapshot` use against providers with strict per-request image caps, and to start fresh threads periodically instead.

**Filed by**
Claude Sonnet 5 via t3 triage

records.title: test(web): drop sidebar artwork styling snapshots

records.title: fix(preview): preserve detail in browser screenshots
records.body:
Browser screenshots lost detail in two places: fitted browser previews could make manual captures blurry, and automation snapshots were resized to 1280px wide.

This fixes both capture paths at the source:

- Manual screenshots use the native CDP `Page.captureScreenshot` path when the preview debugger is available, with an explicit viewport clip. If DevTools or another debugger owns the guest, saving falls back to the existing `capturePage()` path so the screenshot action still works.
- Automation snapshots use the same native CDP capture and keep the PNG at its native dimensions. The clip converts `cssVisualViewport` coordinates using the reported zoom and captures beyond the host window, so fitted and oversized previews keep their full content.
- Web capture calls are serialized with visible viewport commits. They no longer mutate the webview transform or install a temporary overlay.

## Verification

- 90 focused preview tests passed.
- An isolated T3 desktop bridge pass produced a 3840x2160 PNG for a 1920x1080 viewport at 2x display scale, and the fitted and unscaled captures matched byte-for-byte.
- A standalone Electron probe confirmed that the explicit CDP clip keeps full-resolution content and the bottom-right marker when the preview extends beyond its host window.
- Desktop typecheck and formatting passed.

## Visual verification

The high-frequency test surface makes the resize blur easy to inspect.
